subject_line: Townsville and the making of Treading Air
email_body:
Dear Ariella,

I came to Treading Air, your 2016 novel with Affirm Press, through your profile as a writer and lecturer with roots in Townsville, North Queensland, and now teaching writing at the University of New England. I was also interested to see that an earlier manuscript, Hidden Objects, was shortlisted for the 2012 Queensland Literary Awards.

I would love to ask how the long road from that manuscript to a published first novel shaped the book, and how teaching writing sits alongside your own fiction.

The Author Ledger is an independent project featuring short Author Spotlights. The portrait is developed through a few written questions, which you can answer at your own pace, and the full text is shared with you for review before publication.

Would you be open to taking part? No pressure either way.

Best regards,
The Author Ledger

subject_line: Peter Collie and the Amsterdam houseboat in The New Ships
email_body:
Dear Kate,

In The New Ships, Peter Collie is adrift after his wife's death, and his search for understanding pulls him back to troubling events on an Amsterdam houseboat in the seventies, all while the novel stays anchored in Wellington in the months after the fall of the Twin Towers. That pairing of a private reckoning with a world-shifting moment stayed with me.

I would love to ask how you decided to set Peter's backward look against that particular moment, and how the book's moral choices took shape.

subject_line: Polluted rivers and Amazon pools in Where We Swim
email_body:
Dear Ingrid,

Where We Swim moves between solitary swims in polluted rivers in Aotearoa and dips in pools in Arizona and the Peruvian Amazon, and I liked how the book refuses to sit in one genre, part memoir, part travel, part nature writing. I also enjoyed hearing you talk about water and plot with Pip Adam on her Elements podcast.

I would love to ask how you found a shape for a book built from so many separate swims.
